messages:
ravi: Quick follow-up to yesterday's RFC — I'm sketching a small proposal for a 'granular swapout streaming' path for safetensors + sharded checkpoints. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and a minimal compatibility shim.

amy: +1. We need atomic visibility for in-flight loads. How do we handle partial shard failures?

ravi: Plan: index-first manifest that points to byte ranges per tensor/chunk. We stream segments, validate per-segment checksum. If a segment fails, the loader rolls back any mapped segments and falls back to the full-mmap path. That keeps the runtime safe without complex two-phase commit across shards.

ken: What about memory accounting when moving pinned KV cache and activations during swapout?

ravi: Two-level accounting: 1) transient reservation (resident virtual pages / staging buffer) for the incoming segment, 2) commit phase where we move to GPU page-locked buffer and mark as "owned" by the allocator. Commit only succeeds if the reservation can be atomically converted; otherwise it triggers eviction/backpressure and a retry policy.

sara: The eviction signal needs an async hook so the serving runtime can pause new requests for that model instance (or answer with fallback variant).

amy: And we should expose metrics: segment_load_latency, commit_failures, fallback_rate, concurrent_loads. Those will help tune defaults.

ravi: Minimal API sketch I had in mind:

```
load_segment(manifest_uri, shard_id, byte_range, checksum_opt) -> SegmentLoadHandle
SegmentLoadHandle.commit() -> {success, retry, fallback}  # commit moves to pinned allocation
SegmentLoadHandle.cancel()  # abort and cleanup staging resources
```

loader-bot: deploy:started model-loader/streamer v0.5.2

ken: One practical issue: safetensors doesn't have per-tensor CRC today. We can put SHA256 per-range in the manifest, but hashing cost on load matters.

ravi: Right — we plan to make checksum optional. When present we verify async on worker threads. Microbenchmarks: ~5ms SHA256 for a 4MB segment on a standard nvme instance — acceptable for cold loads but we should avoid on hot critical paths.

sara: For Private deployments we also need manifest signing with customer KMS to ensure provenance.

amy: Backwards compatibility question: if there is no manifest, loader should fall back to monolithic safetensors mmap exactly as today. That keeps upgrades safe.

ravi: Tests we'd want: flaky-network injection, mid-load eviction, concurrent reads while commit/rollback happens, and a canary harness that tries tiny models first.

ken: I'll draft a follow-up PR covering the loader interface, the metric names, and a minimal canary harness for eng-sre.

amy: Add a compat-layer flag for overlay dedupe so we don't double-cache the same segment across model versions.

ravi: Great — I'll open the PR and ping eng-runtime + eng-sre for load testing. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
